title: wlanpi-menud WebSocket frame, protocol v1
description: Every frame on /run/wlanpi-menud/local.sock and /run/wlanpi-menud/proxy.sock (/ui/ws through nginx) is one JSON text message of the form {"v":1, "type":..., "id":..., ...}. A reply to a request carries the request's id. A frame the server sends unprompted carries a server id starting with 's:'. Ordering, auth, reconnect and mode rules that a schema cannot express are written out in protocol/PROTOCOL.md and repeated in each $def description.

x-close-codes.1001: Service shutting down or restarting; reconnect with backoff. A restart means a new epoch.
x-close-codes.1008: Policy violation: Origin does not match the device's host (proxy.sock only).
x-close-codes.1013: Try again later: the socket's session limit is reached.
x-close-codes.4400: Malformed frame before the handshake completed (not JSON, not v1 envelope), or a rich hello asking for the default session.
x-close-codes.4401: Authentication failed: no auth frame within 10 s on proxy.sock without WebUI headers, invalid or expired token, token in the URL, or the session was revoked (WebUI logout, token revoked). Always preceded by an error frame with code AUTH_FAILED. Do not retry with the same credentials.
x-close-codes.4426: No common protocol version. Preceded by an error frame with code VERSION.

msg_id.description: Client message id (opaque, unique per connection), echoed on the reply. Server-initiated frames use ids beginning with 's:'.

epoch.description: Chosen at random each time the service starts. A different epoch means the service restarted and nothing the client holds is current.

topic.description: Subscription topic, for example device.summary, complications, alerts, jobs. A trailing .* subscribes to a family.

session_kind.description: default: the service's persistent default session. Its cursor and current view live in the service; it exists from service start and never ends. Any number of connections attach to it: input from any of them moves the one cursor and every attached connection gets the resulting view (the panel's screen is this session). new: an independent session with its own cursor, ending when its last connection detaches and the resume grace runs out.

principal.description: Who a connection is: the identity prompts and confirmations are bound to.

kind.description: local: SO_PEERCRED on local.sock. webui: nginx auth_request headers on proxy.sock. jwt: core JWT in the first frame on proxy.sock.

did.description: Core device id the session acts as in core.

param_value.description: A parameter value. Adapter parameters take {iface, namespace}.

auth.description: C to S. Must be the first frame on proxy.sock when nginx did not attach WebUI session headers, and must arrive within 10 s. Never sent on local.sock (kernel peer credentials are used) or by pre-authenticated WebUI sessions. ?token= in the URL is refused. Success: the server sends welcome after hello. Failure: error AUTH_FAILED, then close 4401.

token.description: A wlanpi-core JWT. Validated with core's introspection endpoint; the result is cached for at most 60 s or until exp.

hello.description: C to S. First frame on local.sock and on pre-authenticated proxy.sock sessions; second frame after auth otherwise. Any other frame before hello is answered with error VERSION (fatal). Declares the client mode (thin or rich), which session to join, what it can render, the protocol versions it speaks and, when reconnecting, the epoch and per-topic sequence numbers it last saw.

mode.description: thin: the server holds the nav cursor and pushes view frames; the client sends input. rich: the client navigates the menu tree locally and sends invoke; the server sends no view frames.

session.description: default: attach to the persistent default session (thin only; a rich hello with session default is refused BAD_REQUEST, close 4400). new: open an independent session with its own cursor. Omitted: default for thin, new for rich, so a client written before this field existed keeps working.

protocol.description: Protocol versions the client speaks. The server picks the highest common one, or replies error VERSION and closes 4426.

screen.description: Usable area. Thin clients use it so the server can page lists to fit (the panel is 128x128 pixels, about 8 rows of 16 characters).

blocks.description: Block types the client renders natively. Anything else it renders from the block's text fallback. text is always supported.

keys.description: Thin mode: input keys the device has.

resume.description: Reconnect state. If epoch equals the server's current epoch and every listed topic's seq equals the server's latest seq for that topic, the session continues (welcome.resumed=true) and the client's jobs stay attached. Otherwise the server sends a full snapshot: menu, one event with snapshot=true per subscribed topic, and a job frame for each of the session's live jobs. There is no replay buffer. On the default session the cursor and view always continue (they live in the service); what resumes is this connection's topic stream: the topics listed in seq are subscribed again, and resumed=true when every listed seq is the server's latest.

surface.description: Additive (complications.2). Display profile an independent thin session's home view uses. Omitted: derived from client.name (wlanpi-fpms: panel, wlanpi-menu-tui: tui, wlanpi-webui: webui), else default. The default session always uses panel and panel.strip.

ephemeral.description: Additive (complications.2). true: the independent session is dropped at disconnect with no resume grace (one-shot providers and CLIs). Refused BAD_REQUEST (close 4400) with session default.

subscribe.description: C to S. Start receiving event frames for topics. The server replies with one event snapshot (snapshot=true) per newly subscribed topic, each carrying the request id.

unsubscribe.description: C to S. Stop receiving event frames for topics. No reply on success.

input.description: C to S, thin mode only (a rich session sending input gets error BAD_REQUEST). A button event against this session's own cursor; other sessions are unaffected. The server answers with a view frame carrying the request id (or a prompt frame when the input opened one).

invoke.description: C to S. Run a node's action. Used by rich clients, and by thin clients for shortcuts. The reply is a job frame with state queued (or a shared running job) carrying the request id and the job_id. Missing parameters are asked for with prompt frames. FORBIDDEN if the node is hidden for this session or the role is too low.

confirmed.description: Rich clients that already showed the node's confirm text may set this to skip the server's confirm prompt.

answer.description: C to S. Reply to a prompt. Only the session and principal the prompt was sent to may answer it; anyone else gets FORBIDDEN. Exactly one of value, values, confirmed or cancel.

values.description: Answers to a form prompt, by field name.

page.description: C to S. Fetch another page of a large result by cursor. Thin clients normally page with up and down; the server fetches on demand. Reply: a job frame (state result) with the page, carrying the request id.

cancel.description: C to S. Detach this session from a job. The job stops only when no session is still attached and the action is cancellable. Reply: job frame with state cancelled for this session.

revoke.description: C to S, admin only on local.sock (WebUI logout). Closes every connection and independent session carrying that WebUI session id (close code 4401). No reply on success; error frame on failure.

nav.description: C to S. Move the session cursor to a node and receive the resulting view. Ancestors are expanded. FORBIDDEN if the node is hidden for this session or the role is too low; NOT_FOUND if the node does not exist.

welcome.description: S to C. Reply to hello. After welcome the server sends menu (unless resumed with an unchanged menu revision) and, in thin mode, the current view.

session.description: Kind of session joined. The default session's session_id is the same for every connection in an epoch. Always sent by wlanpi-menud; optional in v1 so a server written before this field existed stays valid.

resumed.description: true: same epoch and unbroken sequence, the session continues. false: a full snapshot follows.

queue_frames.description: Outbound queue bound for this client.

features.description: Additive. Optional protocol features this server supports. complications.2: the complication.* and complications.configure frames and the complications.live, complications.catalog and complications.config topics. A client uses them only when it sees the name here.

menu_node.description: A node as resolved for this session: hidden nodes are already removed; core bindings and handler names are not exposed.

params.description: Same shape as the manifest's params. $defs segment, param, param_* and confirm are copies of menu.schema.json's so generated models get typed unions; protocol/tests keeps them identical.

provider.description: Set for nodes registered by an out-of-process provider.

menu.description: S to C. The full tree visible to this session, on connect and whenever it changes (mode switch, plugin install, provider connect or disconnect, role change). Always a full replacement, never a diff.

view.description: S to C, thin mode only. The session's current screen as view blocks: a menu list (a list block with selected), a result, a prompt or the home page. Sent after every input and whenever the shown data changes. On the default session every attached connection gets every view, each rendered with that connection's own menu visibility.

driven_by.description: Default session only: the connection whose input (or invoke, answer, cancel) produced the current state, so a surface can show for example 'driven from the WebUI'. Absent until someone drives the session. Concurrent input is last-write-wins.

self.description: true when this connection drove it.

answerable.description: prompt screen only: whether this connection may answer or cancel the prompt. false for a confirmation on the default session that another principal invoked: input from this connection is then refused FORBIDDEN and hints is empty.

prompt.description: S to C. Ask the session to pick, confirm or fill a form: a node's parameter, a node's confirm text, or mid-job (for example core returned needsSelection on a scan and the server lists core's candidates). Bound to the invoking session. On the default session it goes to every attached connection and the first answer wins (a later answer gets NOT_FOUND); a confirm prompt stays bound to the invoking principal (any of its connections may answer it, anyone else gets FORBIDDEN). An independent session's prompts stay private to it. Thin clients get one prompt per parameter.

invoked_by.description: The principal that invoked the job: the only one that may answer a confirm prompt.

job.description: S to C. Job lifecycle: queued, progress, result (first page plus cursor), error, cancelled. Sent to every attached session. A shareable read already running or fresh within fresh_sec is attached to rather than re-run (shared=true). Mutations are never shared.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page; null or absent on the last page.

event.description: S to C. Topic data. seq starts at 1 per topic per epoch and increases by one per change the server publishes; the server publishes only on change. snapshot=true marks a full value (after subscribe, after a resync, or after this client's outbound queue overflowed and drained). When a client's bounded queue fills, its queued topic updates are dropped and it gets a snapshot once it drains; a gap in seq without snapshot=true means the client must treat its state as stale until the next snapshot. The four built-in topics have typed data (topic_device_summary, topic_alerts, topic_jobs, topic_complications); other topics (plugins) carry any JSON.

topic_device_summary.description: device.summary data. {} before the first poll; {"core": "unavailable"} while core is unreachable; otherwise the homepage values, each null when core did not answer. Strings are core's own formatting (cpu "3%", cpu_temp "48.0C").

topic_alerts.description: alerts data: the current alert lines, most important first. Empty when there is nothing to show.

topic_jobs.description: jobs data: every live job on the device, whoever started it. sessions is how many sessions are attached.

topic_complications.description: complications data: one entry per provider app, sorted by app_id, already past its TTL check. label is at most 8 characters (front-panel width).

complication_id.description: Additive (complications.2). A complication's identity. wlanpi.* is built in and published only by the service; plugin.<name>.* is declared in plugins.d/<name>/complications.json and published by the unix user that declaration names; local.<user>.* is ad hoc and bound to the caller's own unix username (SO_PEERCRED).

complication_pattern.description: Additive (complications.2). A family of complication ids, ending in .*: wlanpi.*, plugin.*, plugin.acme.*, local.*. The same wildcard rule as topic subscriptions.

complication_status.description: Additive (complications.2). Closed status vocabulary. ok: working as intended. info: a neutral fact. warn: degraded. error: broken. off: deliberately disabled or idle. unknown: no reading yet. A surface draws an unrecognized status as unknown.

complication_icon.description: Additive (complications.2). A named glyph each surface maps to its own; a surface without that glyph draws none. Adding a name is additive.

surface_profile.description: Additive (complications.2). A display profile name: panel, panel.strip, tui, webui, default, or a new surface's own name.

complication_publish.description: C to S, additive (complications.2). Create or replace the live record for app_id. Only on local.sock, only for principals with role provider or admin, only inside the caller's namespace (see complication_id). A publish replaces the whole record: omitted optional fields return to their defaults. Every publish restarts the TTL. Replied to with complication.ack (state live) or error: FORBIDDEN (wrong socket, role, namespace, wlanpi.*, quota), BAD_REQUEST (schema, undeclared plugin id, label missing on a local.* id). Never publish secrets: every subscriber, viewers included, sees complications.

label.description: Short name. Required for local.* ids; a declared id defaults to its declared label.

short.description: Compact form for strips (85%, -52, ON). Without it a strip shows the first 4 characters of value.

status.description: Default unknown. warning is a deprecated alias stored as warn.

detail.description: Longer text for surfaces with room.

ttl_sec.description: Lifetime from this publish. Default 30. Not clamped: out of range fails the schema.

hold.description: ttl (default): the record lives until its TTL. connection: it is also removed when this connection closes.

complication_remove.description: C to S, additive (complications.2). Remove a live record. Same socket, role and namespace rules as complication.publish. Replied to with complication.ack (state removed), or error NOT_FOUND when the id is not live.

complications_configure.description: C to S, additive (complications.2). Set (show) or reset a surface profile's ordered list of complication ids and families. Role operator or admin, on either socket. Ids not in the catalog are accepted. The reply is an event on complications.config carrying the request id and snapshot=true, sent whether or not the caller is subscribed.

complication_ack.description: S to C, additive (complications.2). Reply to complication.publish (state live, with the TTL now running) or complication.remove (state removed).

topic_complications_live.description: Additive (complications.2). complications.live data: every complication that has a value now, built-in (wlanpi.*) and provider, sorted by app_id. Order is a display concern and comes from complications.config.

topic_complications_catalog.description: Additive (complications.2). complications.catalog data: what could be shown. Every built-in id this device can produce, every declared plugin id, and every local.* id that is live now, sorted by app_id.

topic_complications_config.description: Additive (complications.2). complications.config data: each surface profile's ordered show list and which layer it came from (user: complications.configure, site: /etc/wlanpi-menud/complications.json, default: shipped).

error_code.description: AUTH_FAILED: bad, missing, expired or revoked credentials (always fatal, close 4401). FORBIDDEN: the session's role or visibility does not allow this node, the prompt belongs to another session, or it is a confirmation on the default session that another principal invoked. CONFLICT: core answered 409; message is core's. VERSION: no common protocol version, or a frame before hello (fatal, close 4426). BAD_REQUEST: frame failed schema validation or is not valid in this mode. NOT_FOUND: unknown node, job, prompt or cursor. CORE_UNAVAILABLE: core unreachable or returned 5xx (including AUTH_CLOCK_NOT_SET after the service's own re-mint failed). TIMEOUT: the action exceeded its timeout. INTERNAL: anything else.

error.description: S to C. A request failed, or the connection is about to close. id is the failing request's id when there is one. When fatal is true the server closes the socket with close_code right after this frame.

supported.description: VERSION only: protocol versions the server speaks.

core_status.description: HTTP status from core, when the error came from core.

param.description: Rich clients render a form; thin clients get one prompt per parameter, in order.

secret.description: Never echoed in views, logs or job sharing. A node with a secret parameter is never shareable.

param_adapter.description: A Wi-Fi or Ethernet adapter. The value is {iface, namespace}; bound to 'query' it expands to the iface and namespace query parameters core's namespace-aware routes take. Choices come from core's /network/config/status at prompt time.

monitor.description: Offer only adapters that can scan or capture in monitor mode.

confirm.description: Ask before running. The confirmation is bound to the invoking session and principal.

block.description: Render-neutral result block. Every block carries text: a plain-text rendering a surface uses when it does not support the block type. Surfaces must render text blocks.

level.description: Additive (complications.2). Status of the row; a renderer that ignores it shows the row uncoloured.

priority.description: Lower is kept first when a narrow surface drops columns.
